newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST-Outlook for NZ dollar and interest rates.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Outlook for NZ dollar and interest rates.

text.p: A Reuters poll asked 10 New Zealand bankers, fund managers, stockbrokers and economists to comment on the outlook for interest rates and the exchange rate after Saturday's general election.

The poll showed an even split between those expecting the conservative National Party to lead a new government and those anticipating a Labour-led coalition. Several expected a hiatus of weeks or even months before the outcome becomes clear.
Latest polls indicate Labour, economic nationalist New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance look set to win a majority of seats, but coalition prospects remain unclear.
OUTLOOK FOR INTEREST AND EXCHANGE RATES POST-ELECTION

-- Adverse outcome on the night could spook both fixed interest markets and currency; just as a good outcome could result in lower yields and a higher currency. But too close to call, which is likely.

-- NZ dollar sells off initially, but as long as coalition is Labour-led, will recover, helped by the high rates. Little reaction at short-end with rates around 10 percent; long end should return to yields around 8.20 percent.
-- Hiatus of several weeks post-election will see moderate sell-off in interest and exchange rate.
-- Weakening, not collapse, in both (rates and currency)
-- NZ dollar down slightly, interest rates up slightly.
-- Little significant change unless the Alliance is dominant.

-- If nearly all parties are going to raise government spending (particularly as a percentage of GDP), and assuming the Reserve Bank Act remains intact, then the RBNZ will have little option but to engineer a rise in rates to counteract the inflationary pressures of a massive leap in government spending.

-- Post-election attention will turn to economic fundamentals -- slow economy and declining inflationary pressures. Therefore easing in monetary conditions within three months or so and some modest decline in NZ dollar.

-- Given the strong rally upwards in the NZ dollar value and downwards in bond yields in the pre-election period, if a right-of-centre coalition gains power the widely expected positive reaction by financial markets may be more muted than previously expected, i.e. bought the rumour, sold the fact situation. The NZ dollar/U.S. dollar initial reaction would be temporarily up on an immediate National victory, but depreciating with lower interest rates through November and December. The likelihood of an immediate clear-cut result is, however, lower in our view. Through the political bargaining period post-election, the NZ dollar could be volatile,
depreciating further if a Labour/NZ First coalition gains power. Under this outcome, long-term bond yields could be expected to rise from the pre-election level.
